diagram_math_checks.result: The braid a=sigma_1 sigma_2 belongs to B_3^+; pi:B_3^+ -> S_3 sends it to tau=s_1 s_2. Under right-factor-first composition tau(1)=2, tau(2)=3, tau(3)=1. The arrow depicts pi on this example, not the lift as a homomorphism.

diagram_math_checks.result: Read sigma_1 then sigma_2 downward. Starting top labels 1,2,3, the first swap gives 2,1,3 and the second gives 2,3,1. Therefore bottom position j bears tau(j), and strand k ends at tau^{-1}(k); this distinction prevents reversing pi(a).
diagram_math_checks.basis: def-positive-braid-monoid defines left-to-right concatenation; supplier prefix invariant (d) uses right multiplication to swap the entries at adjacent positions.

diagram_math_checks.result: Exactly two crossings occur: strand 1 crosses strand 2 once at the first level and strand 3 once at the second. Strands 2 and 3 never cross. The continuous strand 1 is over at each positive generator; gaps on strand 2 and strand 3 show the undercrossings, consistent with the explicitly declared local drawing convention. Each pair crosses at most once. No global geometric injectivity claim is made.
